text:
maria.k: FYI customer (AcmeHealth) just escalated — p99 latency for /v1/generate jumped from ~650ms to ~1.8s after we rolled the new int8 quant profile last night. They see it on rw-v2-7b-int8 and only on long contexts (>1k tokens).
liam.s: ouch. do we have metrics? p95/p99 heatmap? :eyes:
anika.r: I pulled traces — backend shows a lot of small spikes during KV cache miss merging. p95 up ~1.1s, p99 ~1.8s, CPU on host not saturated, GPU mem okay.
eng-runtime-bot: [deploy] quant-profile-rollout-2024-11-09 completed on cluster eu-west-1 at 22:43 UTC
support-ops: customer repro steps? is this deterministic or flaky?
maria.k: they sent a minimal repro: long chat with ~1200 tokens, then a single generate of 512 tokens. Happens ~8/10. I'll paste curl they used:```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxxx' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"rw-v2-7b","quant_profile":"int8-default","context":"<long chat blob>...","max_tokens":512}'
```
liam.s: nice repro. quick hypothesis: int8 calibration introduces extra rematerialize or slower GEMM path for large KV sizes; maybe we fell back to a different kernel when sequence_len>1024.
anika.r: logs show kernel selection changed: saw calls into gemm_int8_fallback_path with ~12ms per token vs gemm_fp16 at ~6ms for long sequences. Also calibration step emits warnings: "calibration mismatch, using conservative scaling" for this model.
jeff.p: could be the calibration stats were collected on shorter contexts; int8 scales saturating on tails -> extra corrective ops. We should try toggling fp8 profile to compare and also test fallback to fp16 to confirm.
liam.s: plan: 1) repro on our side using their payload 2) test model with fp8 and with quant disabled (fp16) 3) collect perf counters + nvprof traces 4) if confirmed, roll back the profile for that model in prod and patch calibration. Who can run repro now?
anika.r: I can run a repro on a dev node (eu-west-1) in ~20m. I'll capture perf counters and the kernel table.
maria.k: can you also grab request id and customer timestamps, I'll coordinate with Acme to expect a brief maintenance window.
anika.r: copying the curl, running now. output so far: "p99 1.74s, saw gemm_int8_fallback_path usage spike at step 14"
liam.s: try forcing the model to use int8-compat-profile-v2 (older calibrations) and also test toggles:```json
{"quant_profile":"int8-compat-v2"}
```
anika.r: tried int8-compat-v2 — p99 down to 980ms, p95 680ms. With fp8-profile: p99 820ms. With quant disabled (fp16): p99 650ms (baseline). So int8-default is worst for long contexts.
support-ops: do we have an automated canary check that would catch this? We do perf tests on max sequence 2048, but apparently our profile was tuned for avg seq 256.
liam.s: mitigation options: short-term rollback of int8-default for rw-v2-7b in prod for eu-west-1; mid-term: re-run calibration with long-context traces and add a context-length-aware profile selector; longer-term: improve kernel fallback performance or avoid fallback by updating quantization scaling method.
jeff.p: for immediate rollback I can patch the model routing to prefer int8-compat-v2 for rw-v2-7b, and set a temporary feature flag: "quant.force_compat_profile": true. That requires a quick config push and restart of serving nodes — low risk.
anika.r: also observed some token-level quality diffs in int8-default calibration on tail tokens (small hallucination rate bump), will add to quality regression dashboard.
maria.k: Acme is okay with a brief rollback. please post the exact rollback window and expected impact (downtime none, latency improvement expected).\e ng-runtime-bot: [change] rollback-quant-profile-request created by jeff.p, id QP-4821
jeff.p: rolling at 02:00 UTC; patch will update model manifest and signal pods — no restart required, only a routing table update. I'll monitor p95/p99 for 6h after.
anika.r: after applying int8-compat-v2 route on dev cluster: p95 690ms, p99 960ms. I also captured nvtx ranges and attached kernel timeline (I'll upload in the ticket).
liam.s: follow-ups: - create a calibration job that samples >1k token contexts - add a canary test case using customer's payload - add an alert if int8 profile p99 > 1s for any model-route
maria.k: assigned to jeff.p to execute rollback, anika to run calibration, liam to own canary/alert. I'll update customer.
support-ops: thanks team. Acme asked if fallback to fp16 could be automated when p99 breaches — any thoughts?\e ng-runtime-bot: [note] suggestion: dynamic-profile-fallback is an open RFC on github.com/redwood/serving (PR #414)
liam.s: we could implement automatic per-customer routing: if p99 > threshold for 10m, route that customer's traffic to fp16 variant until next deploy. Should be doable without infra changes — routing layer supports per-key overrides already.
anika.r: one caveat: switching to fp16 changes costs and may affect deterministic outputs. ops needs to be okay with transients.
jeff.p: done with prod patch at 02:02 UTC. monitoring shows p99 dropped to ~720ms within 3 minutes. I'll keep the feature flag for 24h and then coordinate further.
maria.k: I'll inform Acme: rollback applied, latency improved, we will run a targeted calibration and follow up in 48h. :thumbsup:
liam.s: tickets: QP-4821 (rollback), CAL-220 (long-context calibration), CAN-99 (canary test + alert).
anika.r: I'll attach repro artifacts, kernel timelines, and nvprof to CAL-220.
support-ops: closing loop with customer now. Good job.
jeff.p: leaving notes in the model manifest about context-length sensitivity for future onboarding.
maria.k: thanks everyone.
